verdicts.what_would_bite: `gbg round pass open` on any pass after a graded pass whose act and state verifiers disagreed. Concrete path: id X open after pass 1; the fix commit F lands in (head1, head2]; at pass 2 act=HONORED but state=PRESENT, so `fav` is false and X stays open. At pass 3 `pass_scope` sets `fixrange = head2..head3` (Passes.jl:266) and `pass_open` hands the act verifier only that (:450), so F is outside the diff and act can only return UNDONE — "nothing in the diff addresses this finding". `grade`'s honored channel (:611) requires act == HONORED in the SAME pass and carries no earlier act verdict forward (`carried` at :554-556 covers only ids OUTSIDE scope), so X can never close honored, at pass 3 or any later pass, however complete the fix. The only remaining exits are a ledger adjudication or leaving it open — and `unswept` (:301-311) additionally refuses the next pass unless `--sweep-ok`, since no commit touches X's named files any more. Two consequences: correct fixes are laundered into `closed_by = "adjudicated"`, inflating `adjudicated_share` (:668), the rate `gbg fleet --diff` compares — contradicting CHANGELOG.md:105-116's "Rates comparable: yes … none of which alters what a verifier may conclude" for the very change that narrowed the range; and the recovery the design grants the sibling case is missing here — ARCHITECTURE.md:1594 says a seeded id wrongly graded PRESENT "needs no fix and no adjudication — the next pass re-grades it", because the `seeded` channel needs no act verdict, while the identical state-verifier error on a real finding is unrecoverable. The dismissal's own reasoning ("the act verifier is handed every fix range since the finding was banked, or a re-checked closed id is graded on regression") describes a remedy the tree does not implement: `fixrange` starts at the last GRADED pass, never at the banked head. Nothing in test/rounds.jl asserts recovery across passes — :462-464 only check that pass 1's `fix_range` equals `range`.
